plot: The morning after the first snow, one long green line in Wheelburg square keeps melting and growing two hours before Bertha's noon Snow Slide; Grumpy blames Turbo's hot engine, but Bolt's test clears him, the ground is warm, and the line leads to Benny's bakery, whose oven kept going cold all morning (clue planted at the start): grandpa's old hot-water pipe under the square is leaking; Grumpy lifts the lid, Benny shuts the valve, fresh snow covers the line and the slide happens; lesson: when two strange things happen, they may be one problem; cliffhanger: Bertha asks Grumpy to babysit little Tot tonight.

script.title: The Snow Melts in One Long Line!
script.description: The first snow fell on Wheelburg... but one long line won't stay white. Inspector Bolt #27

set.place: Wheelburg town square and the corner of Gear Street by Benny's bakery, the morning after the first snow until noon

beats.say: Snow! Real snow! Wheee! Wait. Why is THIS line green?
Everything is white. But this long line keeps melting!
Last night, the very first snow fell on Wheelburg.
Turbo, darling! Thirty kids are coming for the Snow Slide at noon!
And our slide goes right across that green line!
No snow, no slide? The kids will be so sad!
Just then, Benny the baker van rolled by, grumbling.
My oven went cold again! Three times this morning!
A cold oven on the coldest day. Maybe no warm rolls today.
Oh no, Benny. Is it the snow?
Must be. Everything is cold today. Even my poor oven.
Snow. Cold, white and quiet. My kind of weather.
Except this line. This line is loud. And green.
I know! A space car landed here last night!
Space cars land in circles. Not in lines.
No. I think your engine did it, Turbo. You zoom. You're hot.
Me? I just got here! Well... I did zoom a bit.
Inspector Bolt rolled into the square, slowly, on his new snow tyres.
Good morning. Nobody is guilty until we test it. Procedure.
Turbo, please drive one big circle in the fresh snow. Fast.
Turbo zoomed a big circle. Vroom! Round and round he went.
Look! The snow is still white! I'm not a heater!
Correct. A hot engine passing by melts almost nothing.
But snow can melt from above. Or from below.
Bolt! Bolt! The green line is getting wider! Look!
At breakfast it was thin like me. Now it's Turbo-wide!
Two hours to noon! If it grows, the Snow Slide is cancelled!
Then we must find where it starts. Everyone, follow the line.
So the cars followed the green line across the square.
I don't follow lines. Lines follow me.
Grumpy, you're standing on it. Your tyres are all wet!
Wet? Snow is not wet. Snow is dry and cold.
Precisely. But this ground is wet. And... warm.
Put your tyre right here, Pip. Gently.
Ooh! It feels like a bath! The ground is warm!
Warm ground in winter? Is there a volcano under Wheelburg?
A volcano? Oh my wheels! Under my bus stop?
No volcano, Bertha. Volcanoes are not this polite.
The line ran straight. Past the bench. Past the lamp post.
And then it turned left, towards Gear Street.
It's going to the bakery! To Benny's bakery!
Benny melted the snow? With what? His rolls?
Super hot rolls! Rolling under the street at night!
Hmm. Benny's oven kept going cold all morning.
And our line kept growing all morning. On the same street.
Benny came out of the bakery, looking very worried.
Bolt! Now my oven is ice cold. And my floor is wet!
If my oven stays cold, Wheelburg gets no bread tomorrow!
No bread AND no Snow Slide? On the first snow day?
Benny, tell me. How does your old oven stay hot?
Hot water. It runs in an old pipe under the square.
My grandpa put it there, to keep the bakery warm.
Under the square. Exactly under our green line.
The pipe has a little leak. Hot water comes out.
It melts the snow. And your oven loses its heat.
So the cold oven and the green line are ONE problem!
And I'm not a heater! I knew it!
I said it was you, Turbo. I'm sorry.
That's okay, Grumpy. I zoom a lot. I'd guess me too.
Benny, where can we shut the water off?
Under the old lid on the corner. But it's very heavy.
Heavy? That's my favourite word.
Grumpy hooked the old lid with his tow hook. And pulled. Clunk!
Benny turned the little red wheel. Squeak. Squeak. Hiss... stop.
Listen! No more hissing!
And now, my strong yellow tape. Wrap, wrap, wrap.
A plumber comes tomorrow. And look! My oven is hot again!
And then it started to snow again. Big, soft flakes.
By noon, the green line was white like everything else.
Kids, ready? One, two, three... slide! Wheeee!
Benny brought a tray of warm rolls for everyone.
Fresh and warm! Thanks to a very careful inspector.
When two strange things happen, they may be one problem.
One problem, two clues! I'll remember that!
That evening, Bertha came to Grumpy with a big favour.
Grumpy, could you look after my little cousin Tot tonight?
Me? Babysit? A tiny car? All night long?
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
